Hi Elena / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the next steps we promised on the call so your security & compliance team can review: 

1) PII handling & masking
- Redwood does not persist customer-provided PII in any cleartext application logs. For hosted API usage we store request/response metadata and a truncated token-level usage record. If you need full request body retention for debugging we can enable it under a controlled retention window and with explicit contract terms.

2) Audit logs (what we capture)
- Events captured: principal_id (internal user or API key), action (e.g., model.generate, model.load, admin.key.rotate), resource (model id, project id), timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, client_ip, outcome (success/error).
- For developer convenience we also include a hashed identifier for end-user ids to support correlation without revealing raw PII.

3) Retention options
- Hosted (default): 90 days for detailed request logs; aggregated billing/usage retained for 13 months.
- Dedicated / Private: configurable retention; typical enterprise contract can extend to 365+ days.

4) Export & evidence delivery
- Exports available via the Console (CSV/NDJSON) and an Audit Logs API (GET /v1/audit/logs?format=ndjson&start=YYYY-MM-DD&end=YYYY-MM-DD).
- We can deliver encrypted NDJSON exports to your S3 bucket or provide a signed download link.

Action items (we'll take these):
- Rafael: prepare a 30-day sample export (redacted) and the audit schema CSV for GFH.
- Aisha: provide the retention policy summary and the steps to request extended retention.

I'll attach the sample files in a follow-up email (Rafael will send the technical dump). If you want to add anyone from security as CC (security@greenfieldhealth.com) let us know.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Hi Elena / Sam —

Attaching the items Aisha promised. Notes below on format and controls.

Attachments (stubbed):
- sample_audit_export_2026-05.ndjson (NDJSON, 30-day redacted sample)
- redwood_audit_schema_v1.csv (schema: field, type, example)
- retention_policy_summary.pdf (summary of default retention and contract options)

Quick technical clarifications: 
- Fields included in each event (exact names you'll see in the export):
  * timestamp (string, ISO8601)
  * request_id (string)
  * principal_id (string, internal user or api_key_id)
  * end_user_hash (string, sha256 hex) -- this is not raw PII
  * action (string)
  * resource (string)
  * client_ip (string)
  * outcome (string)
  * metadata (json string) -- contains model_id, latency_ms, token_count

- PII: Exports never include raw customer-provided end-user PII unless you explicitly request full payload retention under a signed agreement. By default we provide end_user_hash for correlation.

- Chain of custody / controls:
  * Exports may be initiated via Console (web UI) by users with the Audit Viewer or Admin role, or programmatically via the Audit Logs API authenticated with an Admin-scoped API key.
  * Exports to customer S3 are delivered using a pre-signed Put URL that is rotated per export. We can enable server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) on delivery.
  * All export actions are themselves recorded in the audit log (who requested, timestamp, destination).

- Retention:
  * Hosted default: 90 days for request-level logs; 13 months for aggregated billing/usage.
  * Enterprise (contracted Dedicated/Private): retention configurable; GFH requirement for 365 days can be added to the SOW.

- Evidence: We can provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA / MSA; for immediate review we can share the security package and the SOC2 access instructions.

If the NDJSON sample looks good I'll run a second export covering the exact date range you want and deliver to your S3.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
